criteria.name: Introduction — Identifies ethical issues and broad links to engineering design; discusses the context of ethical issues in engineering organisations; identifies relevant stakeholders when considering the ethical issues.
criteria.reasoning: Identifies several ethical issues, links them to engineering design and organisational context, and includes a stakeholder table covering interests and decision authority.

evidence.quote: Engineering design always trades quality against cost and time, and that trade becomes an ethical question
First, test coverage is being set by the release calendar instead of by risk
These issues affect the stakeholders differently.

criteria.name: Balanced Discussion — Discusses objective arguments for and against decisions on the ethical issues; draws a conclusion on how stakeholders should make decisions about the issues.
criteria.reasoning: Balances objective commercial, learning and professional-duty arguments, then concludes with options and recommendations for Rachel, management, the health department, chip supplier and product engineers.

evidence.quote: Shipping on time protects a real competitive advantage.
The strongest objection is harm to people who have no say.
Options B and C respect every stakeholder's interests better than either extreme.
Company management should fund the skipped tests for this contract, disclose the measured failure rates

criteria.name: Compelling Argument that supports conclusion — The report forms a compelling argument that justifies the conclusion; the body follows a logical structure, with linked paragraphs and content ordered to support the argument; arguments demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues for all stakeholders.
criteria.reasoning: The structure builds logically from issues to arguments, decision rule, options and conclusion. The conclusion is well supported, and stakeholder consequences are systematically mapped.

evidence.quote: Options B and C respect every stakeholder's interests better than either extreme. They keep most of the commercial benefit

evidence.where: How should Rachel decide when to ship?
evidence.quote: Applied to the health contract, the rule stops at the first two questions

criteria.name: Research and Evidence — Arguments are substantiated with adequate references and qualitative/quantitative evidence; research demonstrates a balanced, in-depth understanding of the topic.
criteria.reasoning: Uses reputable references, external cases and quantitative evidence, while acknowledging the WannaCry analogue limitation. Research supports a balanced and in-depth ethical analysis.

evidence.quote: at least 81 of 236 hospital trusts in England were disrupted, an estimated 19,000 appointments were cancelled
Intel had to offer replacements and took a charge of US$475 million
Volkswagen's concealment of emissions defects in about 11 million vehicles ended in a guilty plea and US$4.3 billion

criteria.name: Report Structure, Format and Language — The report includes appropriate sections serving their functions (abstract, introduction, body, and conclusion); maps, figures, tables, and visual elements are correctly used to support discussion; writing is grammatically correct, fluent, concise, easy to read and understand, and uses appropriate word choice; references are well-structured and appropriate, supporting the report’s motivations.
criteria.reasoning: Report is fluent and concise, uses abstract, introduction, body and conclusion, employs tables and a flowchart competently, and follows IEEE-style referencing with relevant sources.

overall: Excellent report: multiple ethical issues and stakeholders are identified; arguments are balanced and well evidenced; the decision rule and stakeholder-specific recommendations support a clear conclusion. Minor acknowledged analogue limitation in WannaCry use does not undermine the analysis.

feedback.summary: You achieved the top mark in every criterion. Your report names several ethical issues, ties them to engineering design and organisational context, and maps stakeholders in Table 1. Arguments for and against shipping are balanced and evidenced with quantitative external cases, and Figure 1's decision rule leads logically to options B and C and stakeholder-specific recommendations. Keep the explicit acknowledgement of the WannaCry analogue's limits — that candour strengthens the analysis.
next_steps: Sustain the Excellent standard by keeping every conclusion sentence traceable to a named argument, as you do when you say Options B and C 'respect every stakeholder's interests better than either extreme'.

In RECOMMENDATIONS, add one line per stakeholder linking the recommendation back to the specific argument it answers, so the management, health department, chip supplier and product engineer actions read as a matched set.
Keep using Table 1, Table 2 and Figure 1 to carry argumentative weight rather than decorate; when you next revise, check each visual is referenced in the text at the point it advances the case.

criteria.C1: You open by framing design trade-offs as ethical ('Engineering design always trades quality against cost and time'), name test coverage being set by the release calendar, and Table 1 maps each stakeholder's interest and decision authority. Excellent requires both organisational context and stakeholder interest, and you show both. To hold this level, keep each stakeholder row explicitly tied to one of the three issues you list.
criteria.C2: You balance the commercial case ('Shipping on time protects a real competitive advantage') against harm ('The strongest objection is harm to people who have no say'), then weigh Options B and C and give recommendations for Rachel, management, the health department, the chip supplier and product engineers. Excellent requires depth plus multi-stakeholder recommendations, which you meet. Next time, state in one sentence why B and C beat A and D.
criteria.C3: Your structure builds cleanly from issues to arguments to the decision rule in Figure 1 to options and conclusion, and 'Three ethical issues follow' signposts the path. The conclusion is well supported and stakeholder consequences are mapped systematically, meeting Excellent. To keep this, ensure each recommendation in RECOMMENDATIONS names the argument it resolves.
criteria.C4: You substantiate claims with quantitative evidence — 81 of 236 trusts disrupted and 19,000 appointments cancelled, Intel's US$475 million charge, Volkswagen's US$4.3 billion — and you explicitly acknowledge the WannaCry analogue's limits. Excellent requires both qualitative and quantitative evidence plus balanced, in-depth research, which you demonstrate. Continue flagging where an analogue only partly fits.
criteria.C5: Your report is fluent and concise, uses abstract, introduction, body and conclusion, deploys Table 1, Table 2 and the Figure 1 flowchart competently, and follows IEEE-style referencing with relevant sources. That meets Excellent. To sustain it, keep each visual referenced in the text exactly where it advances the argument, and keep reference entries matched to the claims they support.
